title: 2025 Kodiak Commercial Salmon Season Summary
note: Official KMA commercial harvest. Excludes personal use and ADF&G test fishery. Not week-by-district (no 2025 AMR).
run_notes: Chinook harvest 1,315 — lowest in 43 years except 1989; Karluk weir 93, Ayakulik weir 444.
Northwest Kodiak, Inner/Outer Karluk, and Southwest Afognak closed 1 June through 5 July for Chinook conservation. Two mandatory 33-hour June periods before 15 June were eliminated.
Karluk early-run sockeye very weak (escapement 64,469 vs BEG 150,000–250,000).
Ayakulik early-run sockeye average; BEG exceeded (355,800). Two Outer Ayakulik periods before 15 July after BEG exceeded.
Frazer Lake sockeye weak; significant Alitak closure late June and most of July. Alitak early-run sockeye harvest about 19,646; late-run 166,604; district sockeye total 186,250.
Cape Igvak allocative criteria never met through 5 July; no sockeye harvested there through 5 July.
Pink harvest 34,605,698 — second largest on record. Wild-area pinks 24,907,602. Strongest wild pinks Northwest Kodiak and Eastside. 105-hour weekly periods in July; extended time until late August.
Most wild chums average to below average except several Northwest Kodiak runs particularly strong. KMA chum harvest 740,485.
Coho 315,681, well above forecast; majority near Kitoi Bay Hatchery in August and September.
Non-retention of Chinook 28 inches or greater for purse seine, areawide, entire season.

prices_preliminary_2025.source: ADF&G 2025 Preliminary Alaska Commercial Salmon Harvests and Exvessel Values (updated 2025-10-06)
